glossary.definition: A client_id that is a URL. The authorization server fetches that URL to learn the client's name, redirect URIs and keys, so no one has to register the client first.
A public document at /.well-known/poppy.json where a Company lists its issuer, scopes (each with a scope_hint) and APIs for personal agents.
Client authentication with a signed JWT instead of a secret. PingFederate expects the header typ client-authentication+jwt and the issuer as audience.
A JWT signed by the agent's published key that names a short-lived delegated key (at most 24 hours). The delegated key then signs each Poppy-Session.
A header JWT on every request that binds the agent, the method, the URL and the access token (ath), with a one-time jti. It is separate from the access token.

sources.title: Personal Agent Protocol, Draft 0.3
sources.use: Defines poppy.json, the protected-resource document and the Poppy-Session header.

cards.label: Say this first
cards.description: Fabrikam Bank's customer has a budgeting assistant of their own. The agent can use Fabrikam Bank's APIs without Fabrikam Bank registering it first: it names itself with a URL and signs everything it sends.

cards.label: Discover
cards.description: The agent reads two public documents from Fabrikam Bank: poppy.json says which scopes and APIs exist, such as accounts:read, and the protected-resource document names the authorization server. The resource must be exactly the origin.

cards.label: Sign in
cards.description: There is no client id to register. The client_id is the URL of the agent's metadata document, and PingFederate fetches it. The agent proves itself with a signed assertion, not a secret. The person signs in and allows accounts:read.

cards.label: Call
cards.description: Each request carries the access token and a Poppy-Session. The session is signed by a short-lived key that the agent's long-lived key vouched for, and it names this method, this URL and this token.

cards.label: Why two headers
cards.description: The token says what the person allowed. The session says which agent is asking right now, for this one request. A stolen token alone is not enough for Fabrikam Bank to accept the call.

cards.label: Why Poppy exists
cards.description: Today a Company faces two choices for an agent at its door: block it, or let it sign in as the person and do anything they can. Blocking loses the customer who wants their agent to help; full impersonation means the Company cannot tell an agent from a person, cannot limit what it does, and gets bots clicking through pages built for people. Both sides waste effort: Companies build agent detection, agents build evasion. Poppy replaces that fight with a door both sides agree on.

cards.label: What the Company gains
cards.description: Fabrikam Bank publishes one poppy.json and any agent can work with it — no per-agent integration, no client registration desk. The Company decides which scopes an agent may request (accounts:read read, writes only with the person present), which sign-ins count, and which agents are on the allow-list. Every agent visit is identified, scoped and auditable: it can see agent traffic as agent traffic across its APIs, website and company agent, instead of mistaking it for a human or losing it to a block. And because the spec builds on OAuth and HTTPS the Company already runs, adopting it changes no existing system for people.

cards.label: What the agent developer gains
cards.description: One protocol instead of one integration per Company: discover poppy.json, sign in, call — the same three steps everywhere, so the second Company and the fiftieth work the same way. The person never hands the agent a password; they sign in on the Company's own page and grant a scope, which makes consent real and revocable. The agent identifies itself honestly with a URL it controls (CIMD) and signs what it sends, so it is never pretending to be a person and never needs to evade detection. And it gets efficient access — APIs and structured conversations instead of clicking through a website.

cards.label: What the person gains
cards.description: Their agent gets more done, at every Company that takes part, without being handed their credentials. They choose what the agent may see and do — read accounts:read yes, move money only with them present — and they can revoke it. The Company knows exactly which agent acted and on whose behalf, so if something goes wrong there is a record instead of a mystery.

cards.label: Where Ping lands
cards.description: Every step of this flow runs through identity infrastructure: PingFederate resolves the agent URL (CIMD), signs the person in, issues the token with the agent URL as client_id, and publishes the metadata the Company verifies against. The Poppy-Session is verified with the same JWKS machinery. In other words, Poppy is a new kind of traffic arriving at the front door you already own — and the demos in this family show Ping making that door work for agents without a separate stack.

cards.label: What we have not shown
cards.description: The issuer metadata does not yet list protected_resources, which the spec asks for. We found no PingFederate setting for it. UNVERIFIED: that every Poppy client will accept PingFederate's metadata without it.

cards.label: Doctor and health
cards.description: Preflight checks and the demo-health/1 endpoint.
